Cleura is The European Cloud. We provide open-source based infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS), built on OpenStack, with all data hosted in certified European data centers. How is Cleura different from US hyperscalers? Unlike AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud, Cleura is a fully European provider. We are not subject to US surveillance laws such as FISA 702, which means your data cannot be accessed under extraterritorial legislation and stays under European legal protection. Where are Cleura’s data centers located? Cleura Cloud runs in multiple European regions, including Sweden and Germany, with all infrastructure certified for security and compliance. What services does Cleura provide? We offer compute (VMs), containers, storage, databases, managed services, and training — all delivered with a focus on digital sovereignty. Get in touch Reach out to our team and begin your EU-sovereign cloud journey with Cleura - The European Cloud. For support, please visit Customer Service . Use flavors to define resource profiles, attach storage volumes, and configure networking to fit your exact workload. Designed for compliance and high availability, virtual machines are provisioned through CCMP, CLI, or API. Containers Run containerized workloads using Cleura Container Orchestration Engine. Create and manage clusters with the Magnum service, supported by Cleura’s OpenStack infrastructure. Ideal for microservices, CI/CD, and portable app deployments across environments. Cloud Storage Choose from a range of storage types including block storage for high-performance use cases, object storage for scalable unstructured data, and archival options for long-term retention. Cleura Cloud Storage ensures data durability and access control. Managed Services Offload operational responsibility to Cleura’s expert team. Managed Services include infrastructure monitoring, system updates, and backup management. Ideal for organizations that want enterprise-grade uptime without scaling their internal operations team. Professional Services Accelerate your cloud projects with guidance from Cleura’s architects and consultants. We can help with designing infrastructure, migrating workloads, ensuring compliance, or integrating with CI/CD pipelines. Cloud Training Get your team up to speed on Cleura Cloud and OpenStack with our online training programs. Cover topics such as basic usage, automation via IaC, and advanced operations through CLI and APIs. Courses are self-paced and online. Cleura offers a full suite of IaaS features, and services to support every stage of your digital journey. Use this page as your starting point to browse cleura cloud products and services. Click any link above to dive deeper into each category and learn how Cleura can support your specific use case. What products and services does Cleura Cloud offer? Cleura Cloud offers a full suite of IaaS products and services including virtual machines, container orchestration, cloud storage, managed databases, and more. How do I choose the right Cleura Cloud product or service? This overview page is a good starting point. It introduces each offering and links to more detailed documentation, helping you decide based on your workload, compliance needs, and technical preferences. Are Cleura Cloud services compliant with European regulations? Yes. All Cleura Cloud products and services are built on a platform designed for compliance with GDPR and EU data sovereignty requirements. Deployment and data handling remain entirely within the EU. Can I combine different Cleura Cloud services in one project? Absolutely. Services like compute, storage, and managed databases are designed to work together within the same environment, allowing you to build secure, scalable, and compliant cloud architectures. Where can I learn more about a specific service? Each product or service listed above links to a dedicated page that provides in-depth information. pages.text: Cleura prepares AI platform and inference services on Compliant Cloud - Cleura Skip to content The European cloud Support Resources Login / Sign up Free trial! Free trial! Required Invalid e-mail address Max 400 characters In addition to a €50 free trial voucher & tips, I'd like to receive: News & offers Event info Your personal data will be processed according to Cleura’s privacy notice EN Cleura Newsroom Cleura prepares AI platform and inference services on Compliant Cloud November 4, 2026 / Category: News / Author: Mikael Nerde System integrators, software vendors and technology platforms can build their own AI offerings on the platform. Cleura is close to launching an AI platform and inference services for customers and partners. The services run on Compliant Cloud, which Cleura operates exclusively within the EU. They target organisations that use AI on sensitive data. Why control over AI infrastructure matters AI is moving from pilot projects into core business processes. Organisations now need to know where their data sits, who can access it and how they can move it. In healthcare, finance and the public sector, these are regulatory questions as much as technical ones. How the platform works Compliant Cloud runs on the same pure OpenStack platform as Cleura’s Public Cloud. Access requires mutual verification, and only security-cleared EU personnel operate the environment. Data stays in the region where the customer created it. The AI platform is the first step in a planned build-out. Cleura will add compute capacity and a marketplace of building blocks for data and AI development. “Sovereign AI is fast becoming a priority for European businesses,” says Rohan Narula, CEO of Cleura. “Most leading AI services are subject to foreign legislation. Businesses therefore face growing uncertainty over where their data ends up and who can force access to it. Before customers run models on sensitive data, we at Cleura wanted data isolation in place. We also wanted the platform aligned with the EU Data Act and the proposed Cloud and AI Development Act. Auditors will examine every organisation that puts AI into regulated processes, so the infrastructure underneath has to hold up.” The regulation behind it The EU Data Act has applied since September 12, 2025 and gives cloud customers a legal right to switch provider. Because Cleura runs pure OpenStack, configurations and workloads can move to any compatible provider. The European Commission proposed the Cloud and AI Development Act (CADA) on June 3, 2026. The proposal includes a framework for public bodies to procure sovereign cloud services. To learn more about Cleura’s AI platform, visit docs.cleura.cloud/sto-com/howto/ai/ .
